**Issue #1787 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1787: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 40077377349](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40077377349) on `main` (`f50ecdf`, push) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [db (deploy image crates)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40077377349/job/120824021436) | 8m 17s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom: most splits only need a longer matrix list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)`, or `rust (test <group>)`, whose crate groups split further, a crate's test binaries apart with `--lib`/`--test <name>`); for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`. Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`. Make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere (the e2e `WEIGHTS`, a slow test made faster or split across files), and when the split needs `ci.yml`'s matrix, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-8` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40078559081)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`db (deploy image crates)` (ci.yml's `db-deploy-crates`) took 8m17s on `f50ecdf`, a push to main that changed only `apps/web/`. It was compiling the workspace's crates again even though nothing under `crates/` had changed.

The cause: all three image jobs write one buildx cache scope, `deploy-rehearsal`, and a cache write replaces the scope's whole index with the records of the stages that build built. So each run's `db (deploy image deps)` write (`--target deps`) drops the `crates` and `build` records that the run before wrote. After that, `crates` and the binary are compiled on every run. A toy Dockerfile and the real one show this with buildx's local cache, which has the same index semantics. With one shared cache dir, a second run on the same context compiled all four `jackioh-*` crates again (100 s). With one cache dir per stage, each reading the earlier stages' caches too, the same second run took 20 s and compiled nothing.

Done means two things:
- `rehearse.sh` accepts several caches in `REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM`, held by a unit test.
- A person gives each stage's CI job its own scope, using the exact `ci.yml` lines under **Open questions**. The bot may not edit `.github/`.

After that, a run that changes nothing under `crates/` finishes the crates job in well under a minute. Locally, every job in the chain stays under about 2.5 minutes on 4 cores:

| Run | Time |
|---|---|
| deps, cold | 151 s |
| crates, recompiling | 108 s |
| crates, cached | 20 s |
| image, recompiling | 126 s |

## Files to touch

| Path | New/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh` | change | In the build block: `REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM` is split on spaces, one `--cache-from` per cache. The comment above it gets a paragraph saying why (#1787). |
| `apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts` | change | One sentence in the header comment. One new `it(...)` for several caches. |

Do not touch:
- `.github/` (the `ci.yml` part is a person's), `crates/server/Dockerfile`, `scripts/ci-scope.sh` (both files are already on its `db_deploy` and `web` lines), `render.yaml`.
- Any crate's `src/`, `spec/`, `BUILD.md`, the patches.

No spec section or ruling governs this. It is CI only, and the budget is set by `ci.yml`'s header and `ci-duration.yml` (#73). No ruling, no patch fragment (#1565 and #1223 changed these same two files without one).

## Steps

1. **`crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh`, the build block.** Find the line `    set -- "$@" --cache-from "$REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM"`. It sits right under `  if [ -n "${REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM:-}" ]; then`, at about line 183. Replace it with exactly:
   ```sh
       for cache in $REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM; do set -- "$@" --cache-from "$cache"; done
   ```
   Leave `$REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM` unquoted: the word splitting is the point. Add no `shellcheck disable` comment. Do not change the `--cache-to` and `--load` lines below it.

2. **Same file, the comment block just above that `if`.** It is lines 176–181 and ends `# own layers, so any change under crates/ compiles every dependency again.` Append these lines right after it, before the `if`:
   ```sh
     # REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM may name several caches, separated by spaces, each read with a
     # `--cache-from` of its own (#1787). A cache write replaces that cache's whole index with the
     # records of the stages its build built, so while the deps, crates and image jobs shared one
     # scope, the deps job's write dropped the crates stage's records and the binary's, and every run
     # compiled the workspace's crates and the binary again though nothing under crates/ had changed.
     # CI gives each stage's job a scope of its own to write, and reads the earlier stages' beside it.
     # A cache spec has no spaces or glob characters, so splitting on spaces is safe.
   ```

3. **`apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`, header comment.** The first sentence ends on line 4 with `REHEARSAL_LOAD_IMAGE with REHEARSAL_BOOT runs one boot shard on it.` Right after it, add a new comment line: `// REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM may name several caches, separated by spaces, one --cache-from each (#1787).` Change no other header text.

4. **Same file, new test.** Put it right after the test `"builds only the crates stage through the cache and starts no container"` and before `"refuses a REHEARSAL_STAGE that is neither deps, crates nor image, before any docker call"`. Copy the style of the test it follows:
   ```ts
   it("reads each cache REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM names with a --cache-from of its own (#1787)", () => {
     const { status, stderr, calls } = rehearse({
       REHEARSAL_STAGE: "crates",
       REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: "type=gha,scope=deps type=gha,scope=crates",
       REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: "type=gha,mode=max,scope=crates",
     });
     const [build = ""] = builds(calls);
     expect(status, stderr).toBe(0);
     expect(builds(calls)).toHaveLength(1);
     expect(build).toContain("--cache-from type=gha,scope=deps --cache-from type=gha,scope=crates --cache-to ");
     expect(build.match(/--cache-from /g)).toHaveLength(2);
     expect(build).toContain("--cache-to type=gha,mode=max,scope=crates");
   });
   ```
   The `= ""` default is needed: the tsconfig has `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (#1223's build needed `at[4] ?? -1`). The stub `docker` logs `"$*"`. With the old code that line would read `--cache-from type=gha,scope=deps type=gha,scope=crates --cache-to …`, so the first `toContain` fails without step 1. The existing single-cache tests (`"--cache-from type=gha,scope=t"`) must still pass unchanged.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`:
  - New: `"reads each cache REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM names with a --cache-from of its own (#1787)"`. A two-cache `REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM` gives exactly two `--cache-from` flags, in order, then the one `--cache-to`; exit 0.
  - The existing 8 tests keep passing. They cover a single cache and the plain `docker build` path with no cache, which is what super.yml's daily run uses.
- Commands, from the repository root:
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`. Its `pretest` runs `scripts/build-wasm.sh`. The suite's setup imports `src/wasm/pkg`, so a bare `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run …` fails until the module is built: "Failed to resolve import ./pkg/jackioh_wasm.js".
  - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
  - `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/net/deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`
  - `sh -n crates/server/tests/deploy/rehearse.sh` (syntax).

## Done when

- [ ] `rehearse.sh` passes each space-separated `REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM` entry as its own `--cache-from`, and the new comment paragraph is in place.
- [ ] The new test passes, and so do the existing 8 in `deploy-rehearsal.test.ts`.
- [ ] Web typecheck and eslint are clean on the test file.
- [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests (nothing Rust changed) and web tests.
- [ ] The final report quotes the `ci.yml` lines from **Open questions** and asks a person to apply them after this pull request merges.

## Risks

- **Word splitting.** The unquoted expansion splits and globs. A buildx cache spec (`type=gha,scope=…`, `type=local,src=…`) has no spaces or `*?[`, and the comment says so. Do not add `set -f`, which would change the rest of the script.
- **One-cache behaviour must not change.** Today's `ci.yml` and the existing tests pass a single cache. One word gives one flag, and the existing tests hold that.
- **Order of landing.** If the person's `ci.yml` change lands before this script change, today's `rehearse.sh` passes the list as one `--cache-from` value, and the stage silently misses the cache. Apply `ci.yml` only after this pull request is on main.
- **The first run after the `ci.yml` change.** The new scopes start empty, so `crates` and `image` compile once more, as they do today. The deps job keeps `deploy-rehearsal`, so its dependency layer is still found and is not rebuilt.
- **Deploy.** Render builds the same Dockerfile and context. Nothing here changes the image or `render.yaml`.

## Open questions

**A person must edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The bot may not.** Apply these after this pull request merges:

1. In `db-deploy-crates`, step `the image's crates stage` (lines 1188–1189), replace the two cache lines with:
   ```yaml
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal type=gha,scope=deploy-crates
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: type=gha,mode=max,scope=deploy-crates
   ```
2. In `db-deploy-image`, step `the image, saved for the boots` (lines 1206–1207), replace them with:
   ```yaml
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM: type=gha,scope=deploy-rehearsal type=gha,scope=deploy-crates type=gha,scope=deploy-image
             REHEARSAL_CACHE_TO: ${{ (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging') && 'type=gha,mode=max,scope=deploy-image' || '' }}
   ```
   Leave `db-deploy-deps` as it is, still on `deploy-rehearsal`. The three scope names are chosen so that none is a prefix of another.
3. In the comment above `db-deploy-deps`, after `# (rehearse.sh's REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM and _TO).` (line 1142), add:
   ```yaml
     # Each stage's job writes a scope of its own and reads the earlier stages' beside it (rehearse.sh's
     # REHEARSAL_CACHE_FROM takes several): a write replaces its scope's whole index with the stages its
     # build built, so while all three wrote `deploy-rehearsal`, the deps job's write dropped the crates
     # and binary records and `db (deploy image crates)` compiled again on a push that changed nothing
     # under crates/, 8m17s (#1787). The deps job keeps `deploy-rehearsal`, the scope its layers are in.
   ```

**What this does not settle.** A push that does change `crates/` still compiles in `db (deploy image crates)`. In the last 25 pushes to main, 16 changed `crates/` or `Cargo.*`. That compile is 73 s, and the whole stage 108 s, on 4 cores locally. The 17 or so runs of the always-recompiling job since #1739 stayed under the 7-minute alert, since no alert issue was open before this one. Why this one took 8m17s shows only in the job log, which the bot cannot open: [run 40077377349](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40077377349), `db (deploy image crates)`. buildx prints each step's time. A person should check:
- Does `[deps 2/2] RUN cargo chef cook` show `CACHED`? If it does not, the dependency blobs were evicted from the Actions cache.
- How long do the `COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock` step (which unpacks the imported layers) and `exporting cache` take?

If a later push that changes `crates/` still runs that job over 5 minutes, open a new issue with those numbers.

I did not plan a `.dockerignore` that would keep READMEs and tests out of `COPY crates`. It would also change what Render builds from, and it would help few pushes.
````
